description: Issue #943: DistributedLookupCacheService.RefreshAsync<T> is the distributed-cache sibling of the exact defect Bug #804 fixed in LookupCacheService.RefreshAsync -- a caller that times out waiting for the per-key stampede-protection semaphore (`bool acquired = await semaphore.WaitAsync(StampedeTimeout, ct)`) does not hold the lock, so proceeding to Invalidate/LoadFromDbAsync/SetDistributedAsync anyway races the legitimate lock holder's own write and can overwrite a fresher value for the full TTL -- the exact stampede the semaphore exists to prevent, arriving as a lost update instead of a redundant query. This is forced into kind='security' because VALID_KINDS in run_mutant.py only recognizes {'security','selftest'} and this is not a meta-fixture for the runner itself (same forced-classification reasoning etl970-cancellation-classification-guard-neutralize.json already documents for its own non-auth/non-injection-shaped but still production-integrity-critical guard) -- it is not a traditional auth-bypass or injection vulnerability, but a concurrency-correctness guard whose absence lets a stale write silently clobber a fresher cached value read by every subsequent caller for up to the type's configured TTL. This mutant changes the guard `if (!acquired)` to `if (false)` -- a one-line, compile-preserving change that makes the timeout-handling block permanently dead code, so a caller that timed out falls straight through to Invalidate/LoadFromDbAsync/SetDistributedAsync exactly as the pre-#943 code did, reproducing the defect verbatim.

red_expected_assertion_patterns.WalkingTec.Mvvm.Core.Test.Cache.Distribu: Assert\.ThrowsException failed\. Expected exception type:<System\.TimeoutException> but no exception was thrown\.

red_expected_assertion_patterns_observed: Captured from a real `python3 test/mutants/run_mutant.py --mutant lookupcache943-distributed-refreshasync-acquired-guard-neutralize --trx-dir <scratch-dir>` invocation (Release build, stale demo.db under bin/ removed first) -- NOT retyped from terminal text. Read directly from the RED TRX file the run wrote (<scratch-dir>/lookupcache943-distributed-refreshasync-acquired-guard-neutralize-red.trx) via xml.etree.ElementTree, the same parser run_mutant.py itself uses, extracting UnitTestResult/Output/ErrorInfo/Message: 'Assert.ThrowsException failed. Expected exception type:<System.TimeoutException> but no exception was thrown. ' (trailing space is part of the byte-exact TRX text; the regex pattern above does not depend on it). The dry run's own verdict on this first pass (before the pattern was filled in) was UNEXPECTED_RED against the PLACEHOLDER pattern, confirming the harness genuinely evaluated the mutant rather than short-circuiting; the result JSON (<scratch-dir>/lookupcache943-distributed-refreshasync-acquired-guard-neutralize-result.json) records the same message verbatim. After filling in the pattern above, two independent invocations of `python3 test/mutants/run_mutant.py --mutant lookupcache943-distributed-refreshasync-acquired-guard-neutralize` both reported 'VERDICT: KILLED' / 'GATE: PASS'.
